title: Known follow-ups
description: Items deliberately accepted rather than fixed, each verified still live in the current tree. None is a correctness defect in shipped behaviour.

title: workspaceAt collapses every stat failure into ErrNoWorkspace
description: internal/beads/workspace.go:67 discards the underlying os.Stat error, so an unreadable directory (EACCES) is reported identically to one that does not exist. The walk-failure message also says 'at or above the working directory' without naming the directory it started from, which matters more now that errors surface in the status bar.

title: Watcher.Close never closes the events channel
description: internal/watch/watch.go closes w.done and the fsnotify watcher but not w.events, so a consumer ranging over Events() blocks forever after Close returns. Harmless while Close only runs from run()'s deferred cleanup immediately before exit — the code says so — but it becomes a real goroutine leak the first time a watcher is restarted, for workspace switching or a daemon mode.

title: The --version test cannot fail for its stated reason
description: cmd/bv/main_test.go:29 asserts only that --version printed something non-empty, so it would pass on unrelated output. Assert the output names the version. Partially covered downstream by the release check that the published binary does not print 'dev'.

title: Adding a fourth view touches three places, not one
description: internal/tui/app.go spreads view registration across viewCount, the views array literal in NewModel, and viewKinds. Mechanical and textually obvious, but short of a single registration point. Worth collapsing only if a fourth view is actually added.

title: The coverage floor is written in two places with nothing checking they agree
description: MIN_COVERAGE appears in .github/workflows/ci.yml's coverage gate and in Taskfile.yml's coverage target. Both carry a comment saying they must move together, which is weaker than a test. internal/licensing already parses the workflows for other invariants, so asserting equality there is cheap.

title: RELEASING.md still describes the history re-initialisation as upcoming
description: docs/RELEASING.md Step 1 instructs the publisher to re-initialise history and tag. Once that has happened, trim Step 1.1 to a sentence so a later release does not read instructions for something already behind it.

title: ARCHITECTURE.md explains the reload design but carries no measurements
description: The full-reload-on-every-write design is justified there in prose. The numbers that justify it — decode time, per-keystroke latency and the point at which reload cost starts to show — live only in README.md's Scale section. A pointer, or the figures themselves, belongs beside the reasoning.

title: Counts derives blockedness twice for every open issue
description: Snapshot.Counts calls IsBlocked, then IsReady, which calls IsBlocked again. Measured at 0.4 ms per frame for 10,000 issues, so this is not worth doing for speed — only if the duplication itself becomes a correctness hazard.

title: bv hangs instead of reporting when stdin is not a terminal
description: Run from a shell with a controlling terminal but with stdin redirected — 'echo | bv', 'bv < /dev/null' — bubbletea falls back to opening /dev/tty and blocks there forever, before rendering anything and with no message. The user sees a hang, not an error. Found via cmd/bv's own test, which now sidesteps it with Setsid; that fixes the test, not the behaviour. A terminal check at startup that exits with a clear message would be the fix.
